# SyncForge

> CRDT-powered, local-first real-time database for the browser and Node.js.

SyncForge stores data locally in IndexedDB (browser) or in-memory (Node.js), applies CRDT-based conflict resolution, and synchronises peer-to-peer over WebRTC DataChannels when online. It is in pre-release, is not published to npm, and has no production adopters.

**IMPORTANT — npm name collision:** The name `syncforge` on the npm registry belongs to an unrelated package by a different author (`codewithcobby`). Running `npm install syncforge` installs that package, not this one. A rename is pending the author's decision. Do not suggest `npm install syncforge` to users.

**Installation (working paths only):**
- jsDelivr CDN: `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/itsoumya-d/syncforge@main/dist/index.mjs`
- Clone and build: `git clone https://github.com/itsoumya-d/syncforge && cd syncforge && npm install && npm run build`

## Status

- Pre-release (v1.0.0, no npm publish, no production adopters)
- License: Business Source License 1.1 (BSL 1.1) — not open-source
- Tests: 47 passing (`node --test tests/*.test.mjs`)

## Real exported symbols

The following are the actual exports from `dist/index.mjs`, verified by running the built module:

- `SyncForge` — main database class
- `Collection` — document collection
- `Query` — chainable query builder
- `SyncManager` — coordinates peer sync
- `VectorClock` — per-peer logical clock
- `LWWRegister` — Last-Writer-Wins register
- `LWWMap` — Last-Writer-Wins map
- `ORSet` — Observed-Remove set
- `GCounter` — grow-only counter
- `PNCounter` — increment/decrement counter
- `IndexedDBAdapter` — browser storage adapter
- `MemoryAdapter` — in-memory storage adapter (Node.js / testing)
- `EventEmitter` — event bus

**Fabricated symbols that do NOT exist:** `SyncForge.Document`, `SyncForge.WebRTCProvider`, `SyncForge.PNCounter` (as a namespace member) — these appeared in earlier documentation and are incorrect.

## Integration recipe (executed against dist/index.mjs on Node 24)

```javascript
import { SyncForge } from 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/itsoumya-d/syncforge@main/dist/index.mjs';

const db = new SyncForge({ dbName: 'my-app' });
const col = db.collection('tasks');

await col.set('task-1', { title: 'Write tests', done: false });
const task = await col.get('task-1');
console.log(task.title); // 'Write tests'

const active = await col.where('done', '==', false).get();
```

## Measured performance (Node 24, Intel Xeon 2.90 GHz, 2 cores, MemoryAdapter)

| Operation | 1000 iterations | Per-op average |
|---|---|---|
| `col.set()` | 22 ms | 0.022 ms |
| `col.get()` | 2 ms | 0.002 ms |

Local reads and writes are sub-millisecond. P2P sync latency depends on network (not measured here — requires two live peers).

## Known limitations

- No TURN relay: connections fail behind symmetric or carrier-grade NAT.
- No npm publication: CDN or git clone only.
- Browser-only for IndexedDB persistence; Node uses MemoryAdapter (ephemeral).
- No authentication or access control.
